If excessive force is established, it warned, it could erode public trust in democratic institutions.The RDA also flagged Wangchuk’s continued hospitalisation, saying reports suggesting he was not allowed to leave the hospital despite expressing a desire to take leave against medical advice (LAMA), if accurate, raise important questions about patient autonomy. It emphasised that informed consent and a competent patient’s right to refuse or discontinue treatment are fundamental ethical and legal principles of medical practice.The association urged the President to order an independent inquiry into the Jantar Mantar incident, ensure investigation into allegations of excessive force by law enforcement personnel, reaffirm citizens’ constitutional rights to peaceful protest, and seek clarification regarding the circumstances of Wangchuk’s continued hospitalisation while ensuring that patient rights and established principles of medical ethics are upheld.Describing itself as an apolitical organisation, the AIIMS RDA said it remained independent of political affiliations and believed that every individual has the democratic right to peaceful protest. It said preserving constitutional values is essential for maintaining public confidence in democratic and healthcare institutions.
Article Summary: The Resident Doctors’ Association (RDA) of AIIMS, New Delhi, on Monday wrote to President Droupadi Murmu seeking an independent, impartial and time-bound inquiry into the events at Jantar Mantar. The RDA expressed concern over the alleged use of force against peaceful protesters and raising questions over the continued hospitalisation of climate activist Sonam Wangchuk.

Article Title: Delhi violence not spontaneous, says BJP, blames Left
Article Text: NEW DELHI: BJP Monday blamed Left-affiliated student organisations, such as All India Students’ Association (AISA) and Students’ Federation of India (SFI), besides organised groups for protests and violence during Cockroach Janata Party’s march to Parliament.Similar allegations of organised instigation and crowd mobilisation were made in connection with the Delhi riots, and several individuals continue to face legal proceedings in those cases, BJP said. The violence did not appear spontaneous and there were organised groups that initiated it, after which sections of the crowd followed, it alleged.In a hard-hitting statement, BJP functionary Amit Malviya said that the “stone-pelting and orchestrated violence” carried out in the name of students raise serious questions about the intent of the protestors and those backing them.“Even more telling was the conspicuous absence of many of the prominent faces associated with the protest from the march itself, leaving those who had been mobilised at the behest of their political patrons to face the consequences,” he asked. The investigation will establish criminal responsibility, Malviya said.“The real conspirators are often those who plan, encourage and coordinate such violence while carefully keeping themselves out of harm’s way. They move on to the next agitation, leaving those they mobilised to bear the legal consequences.”CJP had been holding protest at Jantar Mantar since last month and has drawn support from opposition parties over its demand for the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan for paper leaks.
Article Summary: CJP had been holding protest at Jantar Mantar since last month and has drawn support from opposition parties over its demand for the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan for paper leaks. The violence did not appear spontaneous and there were organised groups that initiated it, after which sections of the crowd followed.

Article Title: No decision on ethanol blending beyond 20%: Govt
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Amid concerns over E20 petrol, govt Monday said no decision had been taken to increase ethanol blending in petrol beyond 20%.Govt also informed Parliament there was no proposal to make lower-blended fuel or pure petrol available at select retail outlets. It also ruled out any immediate move to introduce ethanol blending in diesel, saying any future decision would depend on evaluation and consultations with stakeholders. "Any move to increase blending in petrol beyond 20% would be based on scientific and technical studies and consultations with automobile manufacturers, oil marketing companies and research institutions," minister of state for petroleum and natural gas Suresh Gopi told Rajya Sabha.He added govt's policy was to progressively transition towards cleaner, technologically superior and environmentally sustainable fuels.India achieved 20% ethanol blending in petrol last year, and E20 is now the standard petrol variant across the country. However, there have been claims of reduced mileage and increased engine wear and tear in older vehicles that are not E20-compliant.Gopi said the transition to E20 had been "phased, calibrated and evidence-based", with blending increasing from 1.5% in 2013-14 to 20% in 2025-26 after scientific evaluation and consultations.Govt also maintained that it had not received any "widespread or substantiated" complaints regarding ethanol-blended petrol affecting vehicle performance and that many such claims circulating on social media were found to be "misleading or unsupported by technical evidence"."Had E20 caused systemic damage to vehicle performance or longevity, it would have been reflected in large-scale warranty claims and service records," the minister said, adding that any reduction in fuel economy in certain E10-designed vehicles was generally limited to about 3-5%.
Article Summary: India achieved 20% ethanol blending in petrol last year, and E20 is now the standard petrol variant across the country. There have been claims of reduced mileage and increased engine wear and tear in older vehicles that are not E20-compliant.

Article Title: 4 Indians killed, 1 critically injured after cargo ship attacked off Ukraine's Odesa coast
Article Text:
Smoke rises from a vessel on fire, amid Russia's attack on Ukraine in Odesa.

Attack on Indian-crewed vessel

Black Sea tensions rise

NEW DELHI: At least four Indian nationals were killed and one was critically injured after the commercial vessel MV Golden Leo came under attack while departing Ukraine's port of Odesa on the evening of July 19, the ministry of external affairs said on Monday.In a statement, the MEA said there were 17 crew members on board the vessel, including five Indian nationals, when the attack took place."As per information available, four Indian nationals have tragically lost their lives, while one is hospitalized in a critical condition. Our Mission in Ukraine is closely monitoring the situation and is making every effort to extend all possible assistance to those affected," the ministry said.The MEA expressed its condolences to the families of those killed and wished the injured Indian national a speedy recovery."We extend our deepest condolences to the families of the deceased Indian nationals and wish the injured Indian national a speedy and full recovery," it said.The ministry condemned the attack, saying commercial shipping and civilian crew members should not be targeted."India condemns such attacks and reiterates that targeting commercial shipping and endangering innocent civilian crew members, or otherwise impeding freedom of navigation and commerce, is deplorable and should be avoided," the ministry said.According to Ukrainian authorities, the MV Golden Leo, a Guinea-Bissau-flagged cargo ship carrying corn, was struck by three Russian cruise missiles shortly after departing the port of Odesa on Sunday. The vessel was reportedly manned by a crew from India and Syria, according to Reuters.The strike triggered a fire on board and led to an overnight search-and-rescue operation. Ukrainian officials said several crew members were killed, while others were rescued. A Reuters witness in Odesa also reported seeing smoke billowing from the vessel off the coast.The vessel is owned by Mumbai-based Ocean Grace Shipping Ltd, according to LSEG data.The attack comes amid renewed fighting in the Black Sea, a crucial shipping route for Ukrainian grain exports. After commercial shipping resumed under arrangements aimed at easing global food supply concerns following Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine, both Russia and Ukraine have recently stepped up attacks on ports, cargo vessels and maritime infrastructure.Ukraine has accused Russia of intensifying strikes on its deepwater ports and commercial ships, while Russia says it has targeted fuel storage facilities and infrastructure linked to Ukraine's military operations. The renewed attacks have raised fresh concerns over the safety of commercial shipping and global grain supplies, as both countries remain among the world's leading grain exporters.
Article Summary: At least four Indian nationals were killed and one was critically injured after the commercial vessel MV Golden Leo came under attack. The attack comes amid renewed fighting in the Black Sea, a crucial shipping route for Ukrainian grain exports. Both Russia and Ukraine have recently stepped up attacks on ports, cargo vessels and maritime infrastructure.

Article Title: Wangchuk continues to refuse IV fluids despite medical advice; low blood sugar, potassium persist
Article Text:
"Sonam Wangchuk being continuously monitored, kidney risk if fasting continues," said Safdarjung Hospital's statement.

NEW DELHI: Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk continues to decline intravenous fluids and glucose administration despite repeated medical advice, even as his blood sugar levels remained on the lower side, serum potassium dropped to 3.2 mEq/L and laboratory tests showed persistent pancytopenia, a condition marked by reduced blood cell counts, according to the latest health bulletin issued by VMMC & Safdarjung Hospital on Tuesday morning.The hospital said Wangchuk's vital parameters remain stable, but he continues to have persistent pancytopenia, characterised by anaemia and low leukocyte (white blood cell) counts. These clinical and laboratory findings warrant continued close monitoring through serial investigations, it said.Doctors said Wangchuk is currently receiving oral rehydration therapy (ORS) and oral potassium supplementation. However, he continues to refuse intravenous fluids and glucose administration despite repeated medical advice.According to the bulletin, Wangchuk remains under the close supervision of a multidisciplinary team of experts from VMMC & Safdarjung Hospital and AIIMS, New Delhi. In view of his ongoing mild to moderate dehydration, persistent laboratory abnormalities and the physiological stress associated with prolonged fasting, sustained medical supervision and continuous clinical monitoring remain essential for his recovery and for the timely identification and management of any potential complications, it said.The hospital said all necessary medical care is being provided and Wangchuk's clinical condition remains under close and continuous assessment. Further management will be guided by his clinical progress and serial laboratory investigations.
Article Summary: Sonam Wangchuk's vital parameters remain stable, but he continues to have persistent pancytopenia, characterised by anaemia and low leukocyte (white blood cell) counts. Wangchuk is currently receiving oral rehydration therapy (ORS) and oral potassium supplementation.

Article Title: Kerala merchant navy man dies in Russian strike off Ukraine ahead of wedding
Article Text:
Russian strike kills 26-year-old Kerala merchant navy man off Ukraine coast

NEW DELHI: A 26-year-old man from Kerala working in the merchant navy was killed after the cargo vessel he was serving on allegedly came under a Russian strike off the Ukrainian coast, people close to his family said on Monday.His death came just two months before he was due to get married.The deceased, Akhil Joyan, was the only son of Joyan and Sally, residents of Vellarikkundu in Kerala's Kasaragod district.Shobi Joseph, ward member of Vellarikkundu in Balal grama panchayat, told PTI that the family received an email from the shipping company informing them of Akhil's death on Monday evening."We are trying to gather more details and complete the necessary formalities. He joined the merchant navy at the age of 19," Joseph said.According to Joseph, Akhil had returned to his hometown around three months ago for his engagement ceremony."His marriage was scheduled to take place two months from now. The bride is from Alappuzha district. He returned to work a month back," he said.Joseph described Akhil as a well-known and respected figure in the locality, who was also a popular tug-of-war player."He was known as a well-behaved and disciplined youngster," he said.He added that Akhil's father worked at an electrical shop while his mother was an insurance agent."They are an ordinary family, and their future depended largely on Akhil. They had recently constructed a house," Joseph said.The family is now in touch with the local MP and MLA to seek assistance in bringing Akhil's body back to India and completing other formalities.According to foreign media reports, Ukraine's Sea Ports Authority said a cargo vessel flying the flag of Guinea-Bissau was hit by Russian forces on Sunday shortly after leaving the port of Odesa. The vessel, carrying Ukrainian corn, was reportedly struck while at sea. The authority said eight people were rescued from the ship.India strongly condemned the attack, saying that targeting commercial shipping, endangering the lives of civilian crew members, or impeding freedom of navigation and commerce is deplorable and must be avoided.
Article Summary: Akhil Joyan, 26, was killed after the cargo vessel he was serving on allegedly came under a Russian strike off the Ukrainian coast. His death came just two months before he was due to get married. India strongly condemned the attack, saying that targeting commercial shipping is deplorable and must be avoided.

Article Title: 'Bound by shared democratic values': PM Modi congratulates Andy Burnham on becoming UK Prime Minister
Article Text:
UK PM Andy Burnham and PM Modi (File photo)

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday congratulated Andy Burnham on assuming office as UK PM and expressed confidence that India-UK ties would continue to deepen across key sectors.In a post on X, PM Modi said, "Warmest congratulations to Mr Andy Burnham on assuming office as Prime Minister of the United Kingdom."Highlighting the strong bilateral relationship, the Prime Minister said, "India and the UK are bound by shared democratic values and enjoy wide-ranging cooperation across trade, investment, technology, defence and people-to-people relations. With CETA entering into force this month, our bilateral partnership is poised to grow even stronger."Prime Minister Modi also said he looked forward to working closely with Burnham to strengthen the India-UK Comprehensive Strategic Partnership."I look forward to working closely with you to further deepen the India-UK Comprehensive Strategic Partnership and advance our shared Vision 2035," he added.The UK entered another chapter of political change as the Labour Party replaced Keir Starmer following an internal leadership contest that ended his tenure as prime minister.Andy Burnham becomes the seventh person to serve as UK prime minister in just 10 years, specifying the country's prolonged period of political churn.
Article Summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi congratulated Andy Burnham on assuming office as UK PM. He expressed confidence that India-UK ties would continue to deepen across key sectors. Burnham becomes the seventh person to serve as UK prime minister in just 10 years.

Article Title: Sikkim tunnel landslide: Nine dead, several feared trapped as rescue operation continues
Article Text:
Ambulance and Fire tenders rush to the spot following Samardung tunnel collapse (ANI)

NEW DELHI: At least nine people have died while several workers are feared trapped inside an under-construction tunnel in Sikkim's Namchi district after a landslide blocked the entrance and triggered a suspected gas leak on Monday.The incident occurred inside an under-construction tunnel at Samardung, Jholungey, in Namchi district. Authorities suspect that around 27 workers were trapped inside, although the exact number has not yet been confirmed.Rescue teams are carrying out a massive operation to evacuate those trapped, officials said."As per the latest official information, seven fatalities have been reported by the District Administration," the Namchi Information and Public Relations Department said in a statement.The bodies of the deceased have been shifted to Singtam District Hospital, STNM Hospital in Gangtok, and Namchi District Hospital, it added."There is a possibility that around 27 workers are trapped inside the tunnel. However, since complete information about the condition inside the tunnel has not yet come in, the actual number has not been confirmed," District Collector Anupa Tamling said, ANI reported."Only after the NDRF team returns will there be clear information about how many workers are inside and what their condition is," she added.The rescue operation is being carried out by the Namchi district administration, in coordination with the NDRF, State Disaster Response Force (SDRF), Sikkim Police, Fire and Emergency Services, the Health Department, and other agencies.The Sikkim State Disaster Management Authority (SSDMA) is closely monitoring the situation, and officials said further updates will be issued as more information becomes available.The incident was reported on Monday afternoon following an alleged gas leak inside the tunnel. The exact cause of the accident is yet to be ascertained.
Article Summary: A landslide blocked the entrance of an under-construction tunnel in Sikkim's Namchi district on Monday. Authorities suspect that around 27 workers were trapped inside, although the exact number has not yet been confirmed. Rescue teams are carrying out a massive operation to evacuate those trapped.

Article Title: No let-up even after strict punishment for rape: Supreme Court
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Expressing concern that there has been no let-up in incidents of rape/ gangrape despite punishment for the crimes being made stringent in the aftermath of the horrifying Nirbhaya incident, Supreme Court Monday awarded a 20-year jail term to a rickshaw puller who had raped a woman in 2016 on the pretext of taking her home from New Delhi Railway Station.In its sentencing order, a bench of Justices Sanjay Karol and Augustine George Masih decided to take a sympathetic approach as the convict was only 25 years of age at the time of commission of offence and had no criminal antecedents. Though the trial court and Delhi High Court had sentenced him to spend the rest of his life in jail, apex court modified the quantum of sentence to a 20year jail term.The rickshaw puller was convicted and sentenced in June 2017, and Delhi High Court upheld the order within six months in Nov. While the convict filed an appeal after eight years, apex court decided the case within seven months. On the first date of hearing on Jan 5, apex court had made it clear that it would not interfere with the conviction order and would only examine the quantum of punishment.The bench said that punishing an offender has a trifold purpose, i.e. punitive, deterrent and protective, and a holistic approach should be taken before deciding the quantum of punishment.“The overall objective is to rid society of criminal proclivity. The same is done by ensuring that the sentence imposed is proportional to the offence or, in other words, not overly influenced by the possibility of reformation and instead, striking a judicious balance between the interest of the victim, society and the accused, after following due process of law,” it said.“In the present case, the appellant convict has no criminal antecedents; was only 25 years old when the offence was committed; given the young age there is a possibility of reformation. The State has neither brought on record anything to show that the same would not be possible, nor has it contravened the statement made on behalf of the appellant that in the nearly 10 years (including remission) that he has been convicted, he has maintained good conduct,” the bench said.The court pointed out that such crimes continue to occur regularly, notwithstanding various amendments to the law to deter potential offenders. While these may have had some positive impact, the need to check such crimes with urgency cannot be understated, it said, citing NCRB data, as per which around 30,000 rape cases were reported in India in 2024.
Article Summary: A rickshaw puller was convicted and sentenced in June 2017, and Delhi High Court upheld the order. While the convict filed an appeal after eight years, apex court decided the case within seven months. The court pointed out that such crimes continue to occur regularly, notwithstanding various amendments to the law to deter potential offenders.

Article Title: NC’s Delhi protest draws oppn flak; BJP slams Omar for ignoring floods, PDP asks him to emulate Wangchuk
Article Text: SRINAGAR: NC’s protest at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi on Monday, led by party president Farooq Abdullah and CM Omar Abdullah , seeking restoration of statehood, drew scathing criticism from other political parties in J&K.While BJP accused the CM and his ministers of being away from the UT even as flash floods wreaked havoc, PDP said the sit-in was completely eclipsed by the CJP protest and asked Omar to emulate Ladakh activist Sonam Wangchuk.“When floods have affected both Jammu and Kashmir regions, the govt should have been here with the people. The protest could have been postponed,” BJP spokesperson Sajid Yousuf Shah said, adding: “The CM should have stayed here along with his ministers to supervise relief efforts instead of attending a show in Delhi.”PDP’s Iltija Mufti described the NC protest as a “lacklustre, deliberately understated and soft-pedalled” one-day event. Her party’s Waheed Parra said the governing party should learn from Wangchuk, who mobilised youths and saw thousands rally in solidarity over the NEET issue. A man without the machinery of govt built a movement, while J&K govt with all the machinery had struggled to build one, he added.However, CPM legislator M Y Tarigami expressed full support to the NC protest. “Its purpose is to remind the Govt of India to fulfil its repeated assurances regarding the restoration of full statehood to Jammu and Kashmir,” he said.
Article Summary: NC's protest at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi drew scathing criticism from other political parties in J&K. BJP accused the CM and his ministers of being away from the UT even as flash floods wreaked havoc. PDP said the sit-in was completely eclipsed by the CJP protest.

Article Title: Global urea prices ease after May spike, fall 40% in June
Article Text: NEW DELHI: The rise in urea prices moderated last month, though it remained 45% higher than in June 2025. As per govt data, international urea prices were $572 per tonne last month, compared to $395 per tonne a year back.In a big relief to govt, urea prices fell to $572 per tonne in June, a 40% reduction compared to prices in May.Industry insiders said this was mainly due to a partial lifting of export restrictions by China and fading fears of prolonged war-induced supply disruptions. “India has a comfortable stock of urea for the current kharif season. We are keeping a close watch on developments in West Asia andits impact on the future supply chain,” a senior industry executive said.As per the fertiliser department’s monthly bulletin of June, prices of diammonium phosphate, potash, phosphoric acid were higher compared to last year. Sulphur saw the maximum rise, being priced at $1,050 per tonne, 265% higher than June 2025 prices. Ammonia prices were also 95% higher than last year.Data shows that domestic urea production in May and June this year was higher compared to the target, offering greater comfort to govt.
Article Summary: Industry insiders said this was mainly due to a partial lifting of export restrictions by China and fading fears of prolonged war-induced supply disruptions. Data shows that domestic urea production in May and June this year was higher compared to the target, offering greater comfort to govt.

Article Title: 1st dengue vaccine gets DCGI nod, set to hit market next year
Article Text:
The latest seven-year data for QDENGA show continued protection against dengue infection (Representative image)

2-dose jab cleared for people aged between 4 & 60

NEW DELHI: India Monday approved its first dengue vaccine, marking a significant milestone in the country’s fight against one of its fastest-growing vector-borne diseases. The Drug Controller General of India (DCGI) granted market authorisation under Form CT-20 of New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules, 2019, to QDENGA, Takeda’s dengue vaccine, for individuals aged 4 to 60 years.The vaccine requires two doses, given three months apart. It is designed to protect against all four dengue virus serotypes.Unlike an earlier dengue vaccine available internationally, QDENGA can be administered regardless of previous dengue infection and does not require pre-vaccination screening.According to Dr Mahender Nayak, head of Intercontinental Markets at Takeda, the vaccine is expected to be launched in the first half of 2027. The company is working closely with the regulator and other stakeholders ahead of the launch, he added. The pricing has not yet been finalised.The approval in India was supported by a Phase III clinical trial in Indian participants aged 4 to 60 years, which found the vaccine to be safe, well tolerated and immunogenic. According to the company, the vaccine has also received WHO prequalification and is recommended by World Health Organisation for use in dengue-endemic settings without pre-vaccination screening.The approval comes at a time when dengue continues to pose a public health challenge. According to Takeda, reported dengue cases in India have increased 11-fold over the past two decades.A landmark modelling study published in Nature estimated that India accounts for nearly 34% of global dengue burden, the highest for any country.According to the company, more than 1.13 lakh dengue cases were reported in India in 2025. Spread by Aedes mosquitoes, dengue has no specific antiviral treatment and can rapidly progress to severe disease, requiring hospitalisation. “All four dengue virus serotypes circulate in India, contributing to recurrent outbreaks,” said Dr Goh Choo Beng, medical affairs head, Southeast Asia & India Cluster.Takeda said QDENGA has been approved in 43 countries, with more than 32 million doses distributed globally through public and private immunisation programmes. Company said it will work with Indian regulatory authorities and healthcare stakeholders to support the vaccine’s rollout.
Article Summary: India Monday approved its first dengue vaccine, marking a significant milestone in the country’s fight against one of its fastest-growing vector-borne diseases. The Drug Controller General of India (DCGI) granted market authorisation under Form CT-20 of New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules, 2019, to QDENGA. The vaccine is expected to be launched in the first half of 2027.

Article Title: Supreme Court seeks more exclusive UAPA, NDPS courts to speed up trials
Article Text: NEW DELHI: To address the grievance of accused facing long years of incarceration in UAPA and NDPS cases, SC Monday pushed for the establishment of additional exclusive special courts to speed up trials in NIA-investigated cases and those related to narcotic drugs registered by various police organisations.Additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati informed a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that 14 additional exclusive NIA special courts have been designated in nine states following a series of SC orders and reminders by the Centre. The courts include three each in Gujarat and Jharkhand, two in Maharashtra and one each in J&K, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Manipur, Assam and Punjab.The bench, however, expressed concern over only one NIA court in J&K handling 47 cases and asked the Union govt to consider establishing more special courts for expeditious completion of trials. Delhi is also in the process of designating three exclusive NIA courts to speed up hearings in 50 pending cases.On NDPS cases, the Centre informed the court that exclusive special courts across the country have increased from 77 to 113, but 394 are required based on inputs from states and UTs. West Bengal and Haryana accounted for 13 each among the 36 newly added courts.Govt said states and UTs have committed to establishing the remaining NDPS courts expeditiously in coordination with high courts. It added that infrastructure needs would be met through existing central schemes for judicial infrastructure to avoid duplication of financial assistance.
Article Summary: 14 additional exclusive NIA special courts have been designated in nine states. The courts include three each in Gujarat and Jharkhand, two in Maharashtra and one each in J&K, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Manipur, Assam and Punjab. The bench expressed concern over only one NIA court in J &K handling 47 cases.

Article Title: J&K flood toll climbs to 28 as fresh deaths hit Poonch, Doda; rescuers dig through debris as rain threat persists
Article Text: JAMMU: Flash floods and landslides fuelled by torrential rain drove the death toll across J&K’s Jammu division to 28 after a house collapse killed seven people in Poonch and three died in Doda on Monday while rescuers dug four bodies from rubble left by raging streams and collapsing hillsides that ripped through Pir Panjal region on Sunday.CM Omar Abdullah announced an ex gratia of Rs 6 lakh for the next of kin of each victim.Poonch accounted for 23 deaths over two days, including several children, while neighbouring Rajouri reported two fatalities. Surankote in Poonch bore the brunt with 15 deaths after walls of water and mud barrelled down mountain slopes Sunday. Four bodies were found Monday.Fresh casualties were reported from Mandi in Poonch, where heavy rain brought down a “dhok”, a mountain shelter built by nomadic herdsmen. The dead included Tanveer Ahmed, Zahida Begum, Shamim Akhter, Shabnam Bano, M Irfan, 17, Manan Rafiq, 6, and 4-year-old Aleesa.In Doda, falling boulders smashed into a bus on Jammu-Kishtwar national highway near Raggi Nallah around 9.30am during heavy rain. Seven injured passengers were taken to hospital, where Manish Kumar died, while rescuers later found the body of an unidentified man inside the mangled bus.In Kashtigarh, a woman died after a shooting stone crashed through her house.Civil administration, police, Army, SDRF teams and local volunteers continued clawing through mud and stones to pull out victims and move families from vulnerable areas.Soldiers built a makeshift bridge from a tree trunk and belaying rope across a swollen stream in flood-ravaged Dhara Sangla village of Surankote, helping rescuers and grieving families carry a young girl’s body home while restoring a vital link cut by flash floods.Amarnath Yatra and pilgrimages to Vaishno Devi shrine in Katra and Shiv Khori in Reasi remained suspended for a second day. IMD issued a red alert warning of extremely heavy rain over the next three days.Relentless rain also crippled transport. A stretch of Jammu-Srinagar NH-44 near Chenani in Udhampur caved in, damaging at least eight roadside shops.
Article Summary: Poonch accounted for 23 deaths over two days, including several children. Surankote in Poonch bore the brunt with 15 deaths after walls of water and mud barrelled down mountain slopes Sunday. IMD issued a red alert warning of extremely heavy rain over the next three days.

Article Title: "Modi Govt has become extremely arrogant": Arvind Kejriwal on Lathi-Charge against protesters
Article Text:
"Modi Govt has become extremely arrogant": Arvind Kejriwal on Lathi-Charge against protesters

NEW DELHI: AAP national convener Arvind Kejriwal on Monday launched a scathing attack on the Centre over the police action against students, calling the Modi government "extremely arrogant" for using force against peaceful protesters.Speaking to reporters, Kejriwal said the youth of the country are "deeply distressed and angry" over repeated failures in the examination system."The youth of our country are currently deeply distressed and angry. Consider the condition of our country's examination system: first, there were paper leaks; then, a massive scam emerged in the UPSC evaluation process, resulting in incorrect scores being awarded to students. Subsequently, the NEET examination was conducted and then re-conducted, yet the entire evaluation system was still plagued by errors," he said.He questioned the lack of response to student grievances. "Students submitted complaint after complaint, but no one paid attention to their concerns. Where are these students and their parents supposed to go? Whom can they approach for justice and redressal? The government simply does not listen," Kejriwal told reporters.Kejriwal condemned the use of force to suppress the protests."When students took to the streets to protest, demanding nothing more than corrections and reforms in the examination and education systems, they were met with a lathi-charge. The government has refused to meet with them or engage in dialogue. The Modi government has become extremely arrogant. Students are being subjected to lathi-charges, and tear gas shells are being fired at them. The protest was completely peaceful and had continued for 25 days without a single incident of misconduct or wrongdoing. Despite this, the manner in which the protest was suppressed today is deeply regrettable," he said.This came as the Monsoon Session of Parliament got off to a stormy start, with both the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha witnessing repeated disruptions over the alleged NEET-UG 2026 paper leak and the alleged embezzlement of donations at the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust in Ayodhya.Earlier in the day, Delhi Police urged people to maintain peace and avoid spreading rumours or unverified information amid the ongoing Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) protest over the alleged NEET exam paper leak.Police also asked protesters to cooperate with security personnel and follow lawful directions to maintain public order.In a post on X, the official account of Delhi Police wrote, "Delhi Police appeals to all protestors to maintain peace, exercise restraint and cooperate with the police in ensuring peace and public order. All participants are requested to conduct themselves in a peaceful manner, refrain from indulging in any unlawful or violent activities and comply with the lawful directions issued by police officers/personnel deployed on duty. ""The public is advised not to believe or circulate rumours, misinformation or unverified content through any platform. Citizens are requested to rely only on authentic sources of information and extend their cooperation to Delhi Police in maintaining peace, harmony and public order," the post read.Earlier, Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) chief spokesperson Saurav Das said they met Union Health Minister JP Nadda and raised three demands, including resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan and compensation of Rs 1 crore to the families of the NEET aspirants, "more than 20 of whom have lost their lives".He said activist Sonam Wangchuk, who is in a hospital, should be "released immediately".Das said that the protest will continue till Dharmendra Pradhan resigns."We met JP Nadda twice. During the meeting, we stated our three demands. First, that Sonam Wangchuk be released immediately... Second, we demand that Dharmendra Pradhan must resign; he should either be dismissed from the Cabinet or resign voluntarily. The protest will continue until his resignation is secured. Third, we demand compensation of Rs 1 crore for the families of the NEET aspirants, more than 20 of whom have lost their lives. We approached JP Nadda regarding these demands," Das told ANI.
Article Summary: Kejriwal condemned the use of force to suppress the protests. Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) chief spokesperson Saurav Das said they met Union Health Minister JP Nadda. They raised three demands, including resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan and compensation of Rs 1 crore.

Article Title: 'Power does not last forever': Rahul Gandhi's warning to police after tear gas, lathicharge on student protesters
Article Text:
'Power does not last forever': Rahul Gandhi's warning to police after tear gas, lathi-charge on NEET protesters

NEW DELHI: Congress MP and Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Monday warned police officers that 'power does not last forever' and 'accountability will certainly be enforced', saying the Constitution, not the government is their 'master'.His remarks came after police used tear gas and lathi-charged protesters during the Cockroach Janata Party's (CJP) march towards Parliament over the alleged NEET-UG 2026 paper leak.In a post on X, Rahul said peaceful protest was a fundamental right and warned officials against 'blindly following orders' to act against students.Delhi Police used tear gas and mild force to disperse protesters who attempted to march from Jantar Mantar to Parliament on the opening day of the Monsoon Session. The protest was organised by the CJP, which has been demanding accountability over the alleged examination irregularities and the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan.In his post on X, Congress MP wrote, "Peaceful protest is an inviolable and fundamental right."Addressing police personnel and government officials, he added, "Every police officer and government employee blindly following orders to attack India's innocent students should keep this in mind: The Constitution is your master.Power does not last forever. Accountability will certainly be enforced."Earlier in the day, Lok Sabha LoP also shared a video message in which he criticised the police action against the protesters and accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi of being 'the most anti-youth Prime Minister in India's history.'He said the students protesting in Delhi were not criminals but were demanding a fair and functioning education system."Tear-gassing students, lathi-charging students is not democratic. It's not India's way and it is not the way this should be done. They have legitimate demands. The prime minister should accept these demands and do something about it," Rahul said in the video.He also alleged that repeated paper leaks had affected millions of students and claimed the government had failed to hold those responsible accountable.The remarks came after police cleared the month-long protest site at Jantar Mantar by Monday evening following clashes during the march towards Parliament. The stage, tents and other structures at the site were dismantled, while police and paramilitary personnel remained deployed in the area.Despite the crackdown, protesters continued gathering on nearby roads and said the agitation would continue until their demands, including the resignation of the education minister, were met. Several protesters alleged they were injured in the police action, while others claimed they were briefly held inside Metro stations and faced restrictions on access to water during the protest.The protest was launched by the CJP over the alleged NEET-UG 2026 paper leak and examination irregularities. Thousands of demonstrators attempted to march towards Parliament on Monday, but security personnel stopped them near Parliament Street, leading to clashes and the use of tear gas and lathi-charge to disperse the crowd.
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi warns police officers that 'power does not last forever' and 'accountability will certainly be enforced' His remarks came after police used tear gas and lathi-charged protesters during the Cockroach Janata Party's march towards Parliament over the alleged NEET-UG 2026 paper leak. In a post on X, Rahul said peaceful protest was a fundamental right.

Article Title: CJP march: Police say detained protesters 'not students'; more arrests likely
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Delhi Police on Monday said the protesters detained during the Cockroach Janata Party's march to Parliament were not students and that their identities were being verified.A senior officer, requesting anonymity, told news agency PTI that Delhi Police had initiated the process of registering FIRs in connection with the clashes, damage to police vehicles and destruction of public property during the protest.According to officials, police are also investigating the motive behind the clashes. They added that even "outer side angles" would be probed.This comes after clashes during which police claimed that stones were pelted at security personnel by the protesters, prompting a lathicharge.Police sources told PTI that more than 100 protesters were detained from different locations, including Parliament Street, Patel Chowk, Constitution Club, Shastri Bhawan and adjoining areas, and shifted to different police stations and temporary detention centres across Delhi.Several videos showing police caning protesters in response to the alleged attack and preventing them from marching towards Parliament surfaced on social media.According to the officer, the investigation has been intensified and teams are examining video footage, CCTV recordings and other evidence to identify those involved in the violence."Those found responsible for attacking police personnel, damaging police vehicles and public property will face strict legal action," the officer said.Police sources said they were verifying the authenticity of all the videos and that appropriate legal action would be taken based on the findings.The officer added that further arrests were likely as the probe progressed and more suspects were identified through technical and field investigations.Police are also scrutinising social media videos and other digital evidence to establish the sequence of events and identify those who allegedly participated in the violence, the officer said.Thousands of protesters converged on central Delhi despite prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), which bars unlawful assemblies except at designated protest sites with prior permission.The march coincided with the opening day of the Monsoon Session of Parliament, prompting one of the biggest security deployments in New and Central Delhi.Police claimed that protesters repeatedly attempted to breach multilayered barricades erected around Parliament Street, Jantar Mantar and other sensitive locations, resulting in confrontations with security personnel.
Article Summary: Delhi Police say protesters detained during Cockroach Janata Party's march to Parliament were not students. Delhi Police have initiated the process of registering FIRs in connection with the clashes, damage to police vehicles and destruction of public property during the protest. According to officials, police are also investigating the motive behind the clashes.

Article Title: 'No prima facie case': HC rejects plea of Mamata Banerjee faction to operate TMC accounts worth Rs 440 crore
Article Text:
Calcutta HC

(With PTI inputs)

NEW DELHI: The Calcutta high court on Monday refused interim relief to the Mamata Banerjee-led faction of the Trinamool Congress (TMC), rejecting its plea to operate three party bank accounts frozen by the Enforcement Directorate (ED).Finding no prima facie case in favour of the petitioners, Justice Krishna Rao dismissed the request for interim relief.The court directed the ED to file its affidavit-in-opposition within three weeks, after which the petitioners will have two weeks to submit their reply, if any. The matter will be heard again on August 26.The ED had earlier frozen the three bank accounts, which collectively held Rs 440.42 crore, as part of a money laundering probe linked to an FIR registered by the West Bengal Police over alleged dishonest financial transactions, unlawful collection of funds, and suspected routing of money through certain party accounts.Justice Rao also observed that the ED's freezing order, issued on July 7, was not brought to the notice of a coordinate bench headed by Justice Saugata Bhattacharyya. The court noted that neither the state nor the petitioners informed the bench about the order, as the central agency was not a party to the earlier proceedings.On July 9, Justice Bhattacharyya had appointed a special officer to facilitate the operation of the three accounts by the Mamata Banerjee-led faction of the TMC for day-to-day and legal expenses.The petitioners had approached the court challenging the ED's initiation of an Enforcement Case Information Report (ECIR), the equivalent of an FIR, in the matter.According to ED officials, the agency's preliminary investigation found that around Rs 160 crore was transferred from TMC bank accounts to Carewell Aviation India Pvt. Ltd. and its related entity between April 2023 and June 2026.The company allegedly routed Rs 82.96 crore to another newly incorporated entity during the same period, officials claimed.Investigators found that a "significant" amount was transferred to the entity, of which Rs 112 crore was allegedly used to purchase an Embraer Legacy 600 business jet and an AgustaWestland 109SP helicopter, officials added.
Article Summary: The Calcutta high court on Monday refused interim relief to the Mamata Banerjee- led faction of the Trinamool Congress (TMC) The court rejected its plea to operate three party bank accounts frozen by the Enforcement Directorate. The ED had earlier frozen the three bank accounts, which collectively held Rs 440.42 crore.

Article Title: Kolkata Chai announces tie-up with Bungalow Hospitality Investments
Article Text:
Bungalow Hospitality Investments, co-founded by Michelin-starred chef Vikas Khanna, and New York-born chai brand Kolkata Chai enter into a partnership (Image/PTI)

NEW DELHI: Kolkata Chai, the New York–born chai brand that helped introduce authentic Indian chai to large US audiences, announced a strategic partnership and investment with Bungalow Hospitality Investments, the newly formed venture co‑founded by Michelin‑starred chef Vikas Khanna and restaurateur Jimmy Rizvi.The deal, announced Monday, includes a financial investment in Kolkata Chai and an exclusive menu integration across Bungalow Hospitality Management’s New York City restaurant portfolio. Beginning this summer, Kolkata Chai’s signature Masala Chai will be rolled out at the group’s current and upcoming restaurants, including GupShup and the forthcoming Punjab Meet House. The partnership will also produce a series of limited‑time collaborative menu items this fall.Kolkata Chai was founded in 2019 by brothers Ayan and Ani Sanyal and has grown through a multi‑unit café model and a line of consumer packaged goods (CPG) chai blends. In 2024, actor and comedian Hasan Minhaj joined the company as an investor and business partner, helping expand the brand’s visibility through media and cultural storytelling.Bungalow Hospitality Investments, led by Khanna and Rizvi, focuses on investing in and partnering with emerging food and hospitality brands.Kolkata Chai is the group’s inaugural investment; Khanna cited a personal connection to chai and longstanding admiration for the brand’s craft and authenticity as factors in the decision.“Chef Vikas Khanna is a pioneer for Indian cuisine on a global stage, and having him join the Kolkata Chai family is a genuinely exciting moment for us,” said Hasan Minhaj in a statement. He added that the partnership reflects Kolkata Chai’s role in connecting people across generations and cultures.The announcement comes amid growing mainstream interest in South Asian food and beverage in the United States, driven by restaurant openings and a rising number of South Asian CPG brands. Kolkata Chai and Bungalow Foods, a CPG line co‑founded by Khanna and Rizvi, have both positioned themselves as leaders within that expanding market.
Article Summary: Bungalow Hospitality Investments, co-founded by Michelin-starred chef Vikas Khanna, and New York-born chai brand Kolkata Chai enter into a partnership. The deal, announced Monday, includes a financial investment in KolkATA Chai and an exclusive menu integration across the group’s New York City restaurants.

Article Title: 'Hopefully govt will fix accountability': Sonam Wangchuk to continue his hunger strike
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk on Monday said that that he has decided to continue his hunger strike after seeing the brutality on peaceful protestors marching to the Parliament.In a handwritten note, Wangchuk said that the his hunger strike will continue until Cockroach Janata Party leaders are allowed to meet MPs at the Parliament or he is allowed to meet them at Safdarjung Hospital."Seeing the brutality with which peacefully protesting Youth are being dealt with, I have decided to continue my fast until the youth leaders are allowed to meet the Parliamentarians at the Sansad Bhawan or I am allowed to meet them here at the Hospital," Wangchuk said."Hopefully government will fix accountability of Education minister before that," he added.He also appealed to the government and Delhi Police to allow the protesting students to present their grievances before the Parliament."I am touched & moved by how the youth have held on to peace despite provocation and I appeal to the Govt & Police force to resolve the issue by simply allowing the students to present their grievances before the Parliament today or tomorrow," Wangchuk said."I'm sure the young protesters will show the same patience and tolerance tomorrow as they did today," he added.This comes hours after a delegation of CJP met Union minister JP Nadda and submitted its petition demanding accountability from the government over the NEET-UG paper leak case.According to CJP spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka, the meeting with Nadda was under way, with the Union minister seeking time to consult the government leadership on the party's demands.The demands include the immediate release of activist Sonam Wangchuk, the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan, and Rs 1 crore compensation for the families of NEET aspirants who died by suicide.This comes as thousands tried to march to Parliament as part of the Cockroach Janta Party's protest call to demand the former's resignation over alleged examination irregularities.Outside Parliament, police used tear gas and mild force after demonstrators allegedly attempted to breach barricades and march towards the Parliament complex. Several protesters were detained.Security was tightened across central Delhi, with Rapid Action Force personnel deployed at key locations to prevent any breach. As a precautionary measure, several gates at Metro stations in the area were temporarily closed, affecting commuters.At least seven CJP protesters, including Abhijeet Dipke, were detained near the Reserve Bank of India, close to Parliament, during the party's 'Sansad Chalo' march, PTI reported.
Article Summary: Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk on Monday said that that he has decided to continue his fast until Cockroach Janata Party leaders are allowed to meet MPs at the Parliament. Wangchuk also appealed to the government and Delhi Police to allow the protesting students to present their grievances. This comes as thousands tried to march to Parliament as part of the Cockroach Janta Party's protest call.
